rv.q: The ensemble acting is the strongest I have seen in years.
There's enough here to make you keen to see what Beresford does next, but I still long for a play that does justice to a decade that changed Britain irrevocably for the better.
The Last of the Haussmans is exposed on the vast Lyttelton stage as a promising debut rather than a seriously accomplished one.

cn.t: Beresford's debut offers strong parts for actors but feels exposed on the Lyttelton stage as more promising than accomplished, covering familiar 1960s legacy territory without making a deep emotional impact.
